description.value: A BC Marine Trails paddle-in beach campsite near Sidney on the Saanich Peninsula; access is by kayak or small boat, placing it effectively off-route for loaded cycle tourers.

address.value: Southern Gulf Islands, BC Gulf Islands, Capital Regional District, BC V0N 2Y0, Canada

raw_osm.description: Gravel tent pads. Hammock opportunities. Pit toilets. 5 picnic tables, food cache bin. Sunny SW aspect. Fee charged May - Sept. No fires, including below high tide mark. Sensitive areas have been damaged by trampling, so avoid overflow camping. Large part
raw_osm.description:approach: Easy on protected shell beach at all water levels. S aspect. Vessel traffic hazards.
raw_osm.description:other: Attractive. View. Extensive trails. Large midden. Gulf Islands National Park Reserve.
raw_osm.name: Shell Beach Campsite (BCMT)

enrichment_extras.reasoning: The specific website URL returns a 404 ('Page not found') because BC Marine Trails has migrated site pages to their interactive member map; therefore OSM tags are the primary evidence source. OSM tags confirm pit toilets and a food cache bin. The site is a BC Marine Trails paddling network campsite within Gulf Islands National Park Reserve, accessed primarily by water.
concerns: Website URL (https://www.bcmarinetrails.org/map_site/12170) returns 404; BC Marine Trails has moved individual site pages to their interactive member map, so website confirmation of amenities is unavailable.
Site is part of the BC Marine Trails paddling network and is primarily water-access only; land-based cycling access is not confirmed.
enrichment_extras.recommended_status_reason: Real, publicly accessible campsite within Gulf Islands National Park Reserve. Water-access-only context is noted but does not disqualify it from a broad touring directory.
enrichment_extras.notes: Capacity is 6 tent sites per OSM tag. OSM description notes no fires permitted, including below the high tide mark, and cautions against overflow camping due to sensitive ecological areas.

wow_evidence: access is by kayak or small boat, placing it effectively off-route for loaded cycle tourers
